name: smartTV for Browser
tagline: A smart-TV home screen that runs in your browser — boot animation, D-pad and all.
ctaSubtitle: Free, runs in the browser, and installs to any screen you point it at.
why: Every streaming service has an app on the TV and a website on the laptop, and the website is always the worse one — a mouse, a cramped header, nothing you can lean back for. I wanted the TV interface on whatever screen I happened to have: the ten-foot layout, the D-pad, the boot animation, the slightly absurd ceremony of it.
how: Next.js and React with geometry-based spatial navigation, so focus moves the way a remote expects rather than the way the DOM is ordered. Motion drives the boot, the focus springs and the screensaver. The only backend is a Cloudflare Durable Object per pairing code, which is how a phone becomes the remote: both ends open a WebSocket to the same room, so it works on any network with no NAT negotiation.

features.title: A real ten-foot interface
features.description: Animated power-on boot, glassy channel tiles that glow and scale on focus, a launch splash, and an ambient clock screensaver after a spell of nothing.

features.title: Driven like a remote
features.description: Arrow keys move focus by geometry, not tab order. Enter opens, Esc goes back, and an on-screen remote mirrors every key for touch.

features.title: Your phone is the remote
features.description: Scan a QR code and the phone pairs to the screen over a WebSocket room. No app to install, and it works on any network.

features.title: Your channels, your order
features.description: Add a channel, hide the ones you don't watch, reorder the grid and pick a tile size. It all persists locally between visits.

features.title: Installs like a TV OS
features.description: A proper PWA with a hand-written service worker, so it runs full-screen and offline-capable on a laptop, a tablet, or a screen in the corner of a room.

features.title: Focus you can actually see
features.description: The spatial cursor mirrors onto real DOM focus with aria-labels, and every animation honours prefers-reduced-motion.
